user.title: ESS Manager - sensors
user.description: Step 1: the sensors ESS Manager reads, where the household usage forecast comes from, and whether to use full-charge balancing. Everything except the name can be changed later in Configure.

data.name: Name
data.price_entity: Electricity price sensor (Nordpool-style, with today/tomorrow quarter-hour price lists)
data.solar_forecast_entities: Solar forecast sensor(s) (Solcast-style, with a detailedHourly attribute) - add as many as needed to cover your forecast horizon
data.grid_setpoint_entity: Grid/inverter setpoint (optional) - a sensor, number or input_number with the currently commanded power, positive = charging (W or kW, from its unit). Used to show Start vs Actief in the Status; with direct control of a number entity it can be left empty
data.usage_source: Household usage forecast source - the next page sets it up
data.enable_full_charge_plan: Enable periodic full-charge balancing (charges to 100% on an interval and holds briefly so the BMS can balance the cells) - its sensors are asked on the next page

usage_energy_dashboard.title: Household usage from the Energy dashboard

data.usage_lookback_weeks: How many weeks back to average (same hour, same day of week)

usage_consumption.title: Household consumption sensor
usage_consumption.description: Point this at one or more sensors that already report your home's total energy consumed (cumulative kWh) - e.g. a whole-home energy monitor. Each hour's forecast value is that sensor's own historical usage for the same hour/weekday, averaged over your chosen lookback window - no derivation needed, and none of the sensor-resolution mismatches the calculated (energy-balance) option can run into.

data.usage_consumption_entities: Home energy consumption sensor(s) (cumulative kWh - more than one if consumption is split across multiple monitors/circuits)
data.usage_lookback_weeks: How many weeks back to average (same hour, same day of week)

full_charge.title: Full-charge balancing
full_charge.description: Sensors for full-charge balancing. The balance is only confirmed when SOC is at least 99.5%, the cell voltage differential is small enough, and the pack voltage has reached the target voltage minus 0.1 V. For the cell voltage differential, use either a differential sensor or the lowest/highest cell voltage pair.

data.voltage_diff_entity: Cell voltage differential sensor (optional, only needed for the full-charge balancing plan - leave blank if your BMS doesn't expose this directly and use the lowest/highest cell voltage fields below instead)
data.low_cell_voltage_entity: Lowest individual cell voltage sensor (V, optional - alternative to the differential sensor above; used together with the highest cell voltage sensor below)
data.high_cell_voltage_entity: Highest individual cell voltage sensor (V, optional - the differential is calculated as (highest - lowest) x 1000 to get millivolts)
data.battery_voltage_entity: Battery pack voltage sensor (V, required) - a third confirmation leg alongside SOC and the cell voltage differential, checked against the target voltage below
data.full_charge_tracking_source: Days-since-full-charge tracking - track it internally (default), or read it from an external sensor that already tracks it
data.days_since_full_charge_entity: Days since full charge sensor (required if using the external-sensor tracking option above - resets to 0 when a full charge is performed)
data.full_charge_target_voltage: Full charge target voltage (V) - your battery pack's own voltage setpoint when genuinely full; the balancing plan treats it as confirmed once the pack voltage reaches this minus 0.1V

system.title: Battery and system
system.description: Your battery and inverter. Capacity, normal charge/discharge speed and min/max SOC become adjustable number entities after setup - you tune them there. The max battery speeds are a fixed hardware limit and can be changed later in Configure.

data.max_battery_charge_speed_kw: Max battery charge speed (physical limit, used by the battery energy forecast - solar above this is assumed exported to the grid instead)
data.max_battery_discharge_speed_kw: Max battery discharge speed (physical limit, used by the battery energy forecast - usage above this is assumed drawn from the grid instead)
data.max_soc_percent: Maximum SOC (%) - can exceed 100% to allow deliberate solar overshoot before discharging

plans.title: Price plans
plans.description:
Two optional plans that act on the electricity price. Both can be switched on or off later in Configure.

**Negative price plan** - when the price drops below your negative price threshold (you get paid to take power), it charges the battery as much as it can during that window, and first makes room in the battery beforehand if needed.

**Spike arbitrage plan** - on a day where the difference between the cheapest and the most expensive price is larger than your spike margin, it deliberately charges when power is cheap and sells into the price peak, instead of only keeping the battery between your minimum and maximum SOC.

control.title: Battery control
control.description:
Should ESS Manager send the charge/discharge setpoint to your inverter itself?

**Status sensor only** (default) - nothing is sent. ESS Manager only decides, via its Status sensor, and your own automation (see dashboard/automation_example.yaml) turns that into a command. This is how it has always worked.

**Set a number / input_number entity** - ESS Manager sends the setpoint itself every cycle, using the charge/discharge speeds the plans were sized with (limited to your battery's max speeds). A new "Automatic control" switch lets you pause it at any time; it also sends idle when an update fails, when the integration is unloaded, and when Home Assistant stops. If you switch this on, disable your own ESS automation so the two don't fight.

The "Planned setpoint" sensor shows what would be sent even while this is off, so you can compare it with your automation first.

control_target.title: Battery control - target
control_target.description:
The entity to send the setpoint to - for example your inverter's grid setpoint `number` entity, or the `input_number` your inverter automation reads.

The idle value is sent exactly as entered whenever the battery should do nothing (usually 0; some Victron systems idle at -30 W).

If you leave the grid/inverter setpoint sensor on the first page empty, this entity is used as the readback for the Status.

error.solar_forecast_required: Select at least one solar forecast entity.
error.battery_voltage_entity_required: Select a battery pack voltage sensor - required alongside the full-charge balancing plan.
error.days_since_full_charge_entity_required: Select a days-since-full-charge sensor - required when using the external-sensor tracking option.
error.usage_consumption_entities_required: Select at least one home energy consumption entity.
error.energy_dashboard_not_configured: No grid import is configured in the Energy dashboard. Add your grid source there first (Settings > Dashboards > Energy), or pick another usage source.
error.control_target_wrong_type: Pick a number or input_number entity.

usage_source_switched.title: ESS Manager: usage source switched to the Energy dashboard
usage_source_switched.description:
**{entry_title}** used {source} for its household usage forecast. That option was removed in 0.3.0, so it now uses the grid, solar and battery statistics from your Energy dashboard instead.

Check that the forecast (the `energy_usage_120h` attribute of the Status sensor) looks right, or pick a consumption sensor in Configure. You can ignore this notice once you've checked it.

usage_source_removed.title: ESS Manager: choose a household usage source
usage_source_removed.description:
**{entry_title}** used {source} for its household usage forecast, which was removed in 0.3.0. It couldn't be switched automatically because your Energy dashboard has no grid source.

Planning is paused until you pick a source: open Settings > Devices & services > ESS Manager > Configure and choose the Energy dashboard or a consumption sensor.
